SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
（印：CONFIDENTIAL）
File No. ............
S.I, Special Branch Station 205
REPORT
Date July 1, 1939.

Subject Soong Kuan Lin (宋桂林) - antecedents

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by [签名]

With reference to the attached communication
dated June 26, 1939, from the office of the
British General Staff, Shanghai, seeking information
concerning one Soong Kuan Lin, enquiries have been
made and the following ascertained :-

60 years of age and a native of Pootung,
Soong Kuan Lin was in the employ of Mr. B. KRENOV
at House 1, 351 Avenue du Roi Albert as "house
boy" for about 10 years until May of this year
when, on the recommendation of his employer, he
obtained the position of coolie at the Lucerne
Dairy, 381 Great Western Road, of which Mr. Krenov
is the manager.

Owing to the state of infirmity due to his
age, Soong Kuan Lin found the work required of a
coolie at the Lucerne Dairy too strenuous for him
and on June 26, he served as substitute for his
eldest son named Miao Seng ( 妙生 ), who is
employed at the office of the British General
Staff.

Soong Kuan Lin has three sons and a daughter,
while at his native home in Pootung he has a wife,
a daughter-in-law and several grand children.
Usually Soong resides with his eldest son in a hut
at No. 7, Avenue du Roi Albert, who is employed as
coolie in the office of the British General Staff,
and who is now on leave. Occasionally Soong
stays at the home of his second son who is employed

as "house boy" by Mr. Krenov at house No. 1, 351
Avenue du Roi Albert and is living at that address.
The third son who is still quite young, assists
and lives with the second son.
According to the cook employed by Mr. B. Krenov,
Soong Kuan Lin has been regarded as an honest
individual who has never allowed himself to be
involved in any outside activities during his
lengthy period of employment at the home of Mr. B.
Krenov.
Prior to serving Mr. Krenov some ten years ago, he
is known to have served as coolie in the Architects'
Office of the China Navigation Company, Shanghai,
and also as cook at the British Military Barracks
in Tongshan Road.
There is nothing in the records of this office
to the detriment of Soong Kuan Lin or any of his
three sons.

BRITISH GENERAL STAFF
SHANGHAI
26th June, 1939.

Dear Sir,

I would be much obliged if you would
cause inquiries to be made into the character of
the Chinese subject whose particulars are given
below, in order that I can form an opinion as to
his suitability for employment as "coolie" in this
office:-

Name:- Kuan Lin SOONG.          AGE:- 60.
Address:- c/o B. Krenov,
          House No. 1,
          351, Avenue de Roi Albert,
          SHANGHAI.

Yours faithfully,

Captain,
General Staff.

Deputy Commissioner,
Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police.
